title: Cell Formatting & Format Painter
goal: Turn a raw list into a clean, readable report: bold headers, borders and centring from the keyboard, repeating a format with F4, copying a look with Format Painter, and fixing #### and merged-cell headaches.

steps.text:
Your numbers are right, but would your manager read this at a glance?

A few touches do most of the work: a **bold header**, a **border** around the data and **centred** labels. Like number formats, none of this changes a single value.

You'll do all of it from the keyboard.

steps.prompt:
The header row `A1:D1` is selected.

Press [[Ctrl]] + [[B]] to make it **bold**. Press it again any time to switch bold off.
clues: B for bold. Hold Ctrl, tap B.

steps.prompt:
The Total row should be bold too. You've selected `A6:D6`.

Instead of reaching for [[Ctrl]] + [[B]] again, press [[F4]]: it **repeats your last action**, whatever it was.

On a laptop you may need [[Fn]] + [[F4]].
clues: The F keys run along the very top of the keyboard.

steps.prompt:
Now frame the data. `A1:D6` are selected.

Press [[Ctrl]] + [[Shift]] + [[7]] (the **&** key) to draw a border around the outside.
clues: Ctrl + Shift, then 7. On a Mac: Cmd + Option + 0.

steps.prompt:
Centre the quarter names over their numbers. `B1:D1` are selected.

There's no one-key shortcut for this in Windows Excel, so use the ribbon keys, tapped one after another: [[Alt]], [[H]] (Home), [[A]] (Align), [[C]] (Centre).

On a Mac it's [[Cmd]] + [[E]].
clues: Tap Alt and let go, then H, then A, then C.

steps.prompt:
You've styled one header perfectly and want the same look on three other sheets' headers. **Format Painter** (the paintbrush on the Home tab) copies a look, not the contents.

How do you paint **several** places in one go?
options: Double-click the brush, paint every place, then press Esc
Copy and paste the header text
steps.explain: One click paints **once**. A **double-click** keeps the brush loaded until you press [[Esc]], so you can paint as many places as you like.
wrongFeedback: That works, but you'd go back to the brush every time. There's a way to keep it loaded.
Pasting copies the text too. Format Painter copies only the look.
clues: Think: what does a double-click usually do that a single click doesn't?

steps.prompt: You make the totals bold and suddenly a cell shows **#######**. Did you break something?
options: Yes, the formula has an error
No, the column is just too narrow; double-click its right edge to widen it
steps.explain: **####** only means “I don't fit”. Bold text and currency signs make numbers wider. Double-click the line to the right of the column letter and Excel sizes the column to fit.
wrongFeedback: Real errors start with `#` and have a name, like `#VALUE!`. A row of hashes is different.
The value is still there; click the cell and check the formula bar.
clues: What got wider when you made it bold?

steps.prompt:
You want a title centred across `A1:D1`. **Merge & Center** does it, but merged cells cause trouble later: you can't sort, filter or select columns cleanly.

What do experienced users do instead?
options: Merge anyway, and unmerge before sorting
Format Cells → Alignment → Center Across Selection
Type the title in `B1` and add spaces in front
steps.explain: **Center Across Selection** looks exactly like a merge, but every cell stays separate, so sorting and selecting keep working. Find it in Format Cells ([[Ctrl]] + [[1]]) on the Alignment tab.
wrongFeedback: It works, but it's easy to forget, and then the sort fails.
Spaces break as soon as the column width changes.
clues: Look for an option that only **looks** like merging.

steps.prompt:
The column headers in `A1:C1` blend in with the data. They're selected.

Make them stand out.
clues: The first shortcut in this topic.
